rationale_bullets: The 2025 three-man rotation (2,434 combined at 58.7%, 17-11) is gone except its best piece: Lewis - 5-star, 589 yds (55.3%), 4 TD / 0 INT in 2 starts as a 17-YEAR-OLD, redshirt kept; PFF 72.1/121 is the best small-sample QB tape in our rebuild cohort.
PS's read is attributed and bullish ('I look for Lewis to thrive in the Go-Go offense'); the Athlon scout's caveat is the counterweight ('how good can he be in Year 2 while still being a young guy').
Wilson (7 true-FR starts at Utah, more INT than TD) is a real battle entrant, not just depth.
45 = fringe-below-average: elite trajectory on 121 snaps, brand-new scheme, no proven FBS starter in the room.
The baseline is dead-last: 0th-pctile as-played, and no CU rusher has topped 400 yards in four years (PS).

The reload is uniquely scheme-targeted: Marion brought his own Sac St pair - Henderson (565 @ 6.2) and Smith (511 @ 6.7) IN THIS OFFENSE - plus Bama pedigree Young (PS#2 transfer RB) and a healthy Taylor (909 @ 6.0 at IW '24); Welch (team-high 384, Athlon-bold) returns.
The scheme runs ~69% of snaps, and PS calls it 'one of the most improved RB rooms in the FBS' (opinion, attributed).
48 = fringe-average: coordinator-continuity evidence for the transfers is the strongest we've seen; zero returning FBS volume caps it.

key_players.name: Richard Young
key_players.evidence: Bama; PS#2 transfer RB; 234 career yds

rationale_bullets: The best verified WR haul of the round: Scudero (74.3/507 - FBS-leading 1,297, PS 2nd-team All-America), Perry (77.3/370 - 976 @ 22.7, 1st-tm MAC), Moore (71.7/263, Texas starter), Campbell (755 @ 20.4 at Sac St).
Returning glue is real: J.Williams (67.7/298; 1,071 over two years) + TE Atkins (used more in the new scheme).
P6: 'the clear strength of the roster'; the Athlon scout: 'they're always gonna have receivers... that's Deion's deal.'
56 = above average: three 70+ tapes + the national receiving leader, capped by QB uncertainty and a run-first scheme.

The fourth straight rebuild: 27 different starters in 3 years; the best 2025 grade (McGill 72.6/798) expired and Seaton left as a 5-star; Athlon's lone bold returner (L.Johnson) is DEPTH on PS's chart.

The incoming eight carry 100 career FBS starts: Hunter (24 st, 59.7/811), White (20 st, 65.6/755), Bell (8 st, 61.9/583), Soto (11 st in Marion's offense), Hughley (UGA, 2 st) - PS: 'Bell and Hughley look like NFL OTs' (opinion).
2025 already improved to the 65th pctile as-played, but output stayed poor (38 sacks) and the scout blames scheming - the new OC is part of the fix thesis.
40 = below average: experience mass + two projectable tackles, no above-average verified starter.
All four starters gone from a unit that allowed 223 rush ypg (2nd-worst natl) with 13 sacks - the floor was already in.

The replacement tape is the best DL haul we've graded: Hopper (80.2/661, 1st-tm AAC), Christensen (88.6/494 - the roster's best grade), Talib (79.0/374), Taufatofua (71.8/454), Manuel (71.4/434) + 375-lb Taumanupepe and 1st-tm CAA Kamara (67 tkl, 7.5 sk).
PS's calibrated take: 'improved numbers but not to '24's level' (the '24 unit led the B12 in sacks).
55 = above average: five 70+ verified tapes stepping up one level, first-year DC install the cap.

key_players.name: Santana Hopper
key_players.evidence: PFF 80.2/661 at Tulane; 8.5 sk at App St prior

rationale_bullets: Wholesale replacement of a 9th-pctile room (all three starters gone; best returner had graded 54.6).

Lampron arrives with grade AND production aligned: 86.6/753, 119 tkl, 17.5 tfl, 1st-tm MAC - after 1st-tm Pioneer at Dayton the year before (a two-level climber; his PFF row was name-corrupted and manually restored).
Lefau (22 starts, 132 tkl at Texas) is P4-proven; Martinez (123 tkl L2Y, 2nd-tm CUSA) adds volume; PS: 'one of the best [LB units] they've had' (opinion).
LB caution rule satisfied on Lampron (tape agrees). 50 = average: massive upgrade from the baseline, unproven together.
Zero returning starters (Athlon DEFENSE (0)); the 2025 quality left with destinations (Byard 75.0 -> A&M, Stoutmire 72.4 -> Arkansas, McKinney -> ND).

Nine transfers, four with 650+ snaps of 64-75 tape: Eaglin (74.7/679, All-SBC), Floyd (69.0/846), Fontenette (68.2/790 - 125 tkl at Vandy, to FS), Mitchell (64.8/845, 2nd-tm CUSA); wildcards Carter (Tenn Top100, 'big spring') and Thomas (ND, 'star potential').
PS: 'stronger at S than CB' - the CB room is pedigree (Thomas rFr) + returners (Vickers) + FCS tape (Omodia 19 st/89 tkl, no PFF row).
47 = fringe-average: real safety tape + the program's DB brand vs zero continuity and thin verified CB play.
The kicker who set the school career FG% record graduated; the battle is a redshirt FR with no tape ('strong leg' - Athlon) vs a journeyman who went 6-10 last year.
P Greaves returns off a 'solid first year' (43.7 avg / 37.4 net - modest); STR history is poor (#111/#97 per PS).
Return game gains Carter/Gibson speed. 42 = below average: half-stable, half-unknown.
